note: Postgres through Drizzle, server-side only, so no RLS findings. Tenant isolation lives only in route code, and several routes miss it (see auth_gap). No ai_browser_call, ai_fake_tool or secret_exposure found. Model calls are server-side, env.example holds placeholders only, and no .env is committed. public/widget/embed.js is a minified build of src/widget, so src/widget was reviewed instead. docs/, .claude/, README, lockfile and components/ui shadcn files skipped. Side bug: the dashboard reads /api/chat/[id]/messages, which only returns chats owned by the logged-in user and returns an array, not {messages}. So agents cannot load widget conversations. | Second labeler: Model calls run only on the server through OpenRouter. No model key is in browser code. The database is plain Postgres reached only from server code, so no database_rules labels apply. Tenant isolation depends on WHERE clauses in each route, and several routes miss them (see auth_gap). No committed .env and no real secrets. env.example holds placeholders. The widget uses /api/chat. /api/widget/chat is unused and fails on new chats because saveChat gets no orgId and puts a widget session id in a user FK. Config fields confidence_correction_threshold, correction_strategy and webhooks.completion_url do nothing: nothing reads the first two, and no code queues a conversation.completed job. Not reviewed: docs/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .cursor/, drizzle/meta snapshots, components/ui (shadcn), lockfile.

labels.what: escalate takes chatId from the model (the route writes the chat id into the system prompt) and never checks it is the current chat, so an injected prompt can escalate any chat by id. No per-chat limit, so repeated calls queue repeated webhook jobs. reason and summary have no length cap

collect_feedback inserts a Feedback row for any model-supplied chatId with no check that it is the current chat and no one-per-chat limit. Only the 1-5 rating range is checked. comment has no length cap
The model writes a satisfaction rating and comment with no customer confirmation step, so a rating the customer never gave can be stored

escalate changes the chat status and queues a webhook straight from the model call. In the Vex path the tools run inside generateText before the Vex check, so a response Vex later blocks has already run its tool side effects

Code detects the escalation keywords but only appends 'Use the escalate tool immediately' to the prompt. The escalation itself is left to the model, so a customer who asks for a human may not be escalated
Same keyword escalation rule written only as a prompt line in the widget route

Default system prompt says answer only from the knowledge base, admit unknowns and always cite sources. No code checks grounding or citations (Vex is optional and the no-Vex path streams the raw answer)
Tool description says billing disputes and account security need a human. Nothing in code routes those topics to escalation
Tool description says always search the knowledge base before answering factual questions. The route sets no toolChoice, so the model can answer without searching

Escalation webhook never fires. The job payload uses type 'escalation' but webhook-worker switches on event and expects 'conversation.escalated', so it returns without sending. The customer is still told a human will follow up shortly. The chat status update is real

conversation.completed and its completion_url are never queued anywhere, so the completion webhook is dead config. escalation_url and low_confidence_url default to empty, so nothing is sent unless set

Comment says PostgreSQL NOTIFY but emitChatMessage is an in-process emitter, and it is passed the message id string instead of the message. The stream listener reads message.createdAt and throws inside a try, so live agent replies never reach the widget or dashboard
Password reset email is never sent. The reset URL is printed with console.log while the form tells the user a reset link has been sent
Verification email on sign-up is never sent. The verification URL is printed with console.log
Edit profile Save Changes only closes the dialog and shows a toast. No API call, while the dialog text says changes will be saved
Resolve button sets the status to resolved in the UI without checking the PATCH response. Agent send (333-346) also ignores the response
Hardcoded account type 'Standard' and session status 'Active now' shown as if real
Hardcoded '1 Active' sessions badge, not read from the session table
Demo page hardcodes an agent public key and a test user email and name

Ownership check runs only when both user ids exist. A widget token (userId null) can post into any chat id. A logged-in user can post into any widget chat of any org (no orgId check), the model then runs on that chat's full history, and on an escalated chat the user is saved as 'agent' and auto-assigned (179, 211-216)
DELETE skips the ownership check when the caller is a widget session (userId null), so any widget token can delete any chat and its messages by id
Live message stream checks only that the chat exists. Any widget token or any logged-in user can subscribe to any chat in any org
PATCH updates the status of any chat by id for any logged-in user, with no org membership check
Customer identity is whatever email the browser sends. It is never verified, yet the dashboard shows it as the customer email. Anyone with the public agent id can open sessions as any email

Widget chat route calls getActiveTools() with no orgId, so knowledge_search uses the null-org tool and searches every org's documents. The route looks unused and broken (saveChat at 94-98 has no orgId and sets userId to the widget session id), and the widget posts to /api/chat instead

Proxy only checks that a session cookie exists, and its matcher lists exact paths, so /dashboard/conversations, /dashboard/knowledge-base and /chat/[id] are not covered. Those pages gate with client useSession only. The APIs do check the session server-side
OrgMember role (owner, admin, agent) is stored but no route checks it, so every member can delete knowledge sources and change chat status
No rate limit on paid AI use. Anyone with the public agent id can create unlimited widget sessions, and each can call /api/chat, which runs the model with high reasoning effort
Server-side fetch of a user-supplied URL with redirects followed and no private-address block (SSRF). The sitemap path has no page cap, so one source can queue unlimited paid embedding jobs
Widget session token is stored in localStorage on the host site and never expires (WidgetSession has no expiry)
Session token accepted in the query string, so it can land in logs and referrers
Client-sent message parts are saved and replayed to the model with no validation, so a client can forge tool or assistant parts in its own history
Password reset and email verification URLs (bearer tokens) are written to server logs
No size cap on file content before it is chunked and embedded with a paid model
Raw user text is joined into the title-generation prompt with no guard

Embedding model hardcoded to openai/text-embedding-3-small while env.example sets OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL to text-embedding-3-large, which is never read. The vector column is 1536 dims, which only fits the small model
OPENROUTER_MODEL defaults to openai/gpt-5-mini here, env.example sets anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, and the chat route never reads it (it uses agent config model.provider)
Vex agentId hardcoded to 'vex-customer-support' here and at line 199, while config vex.agent_id is 'my-support-bot' and is sent in webhook payloads. Two values for one id

Widget hardcodes #0066FF (also line 130), the 'Support' title (794) and the email gate (466). It ignores the branding, welcome_message, position and require_email_if_anonymous config and the org overrides
confidence_correction_threshold is configurable but never read anywhere
getActiveTools reads only the global config.tools, so per-org toolsEnabled overrides never take effect
stepCountIs(5) and reasoning effort 'high' hardcoded and repeated at 347-351 and 364-368 (and in the widget route)
localhost:3000 fallback for the auth base URL in client code. Same fallback in env.ts 41, sitemap.ts 4, robots.ts 4, and redis localhost in env.ts 28 and connection.ts 8
Widget script src points to http://localhost:3000
Dev database user and password in the compose file, with Postgres and Redis ports published
Any logged-in user from any org who posts to an escalated chat is saved with role agent and auto-assigned as the agent. There is no org membership or role check.

When getActiveTools() is called with no orgId (widget chat route line 137), knowledge_search uses orgId null and searchKnowledgeBase (retrieval.ts lines 36-46) searches every org's documents. The widget chat route is broken for new chats, so reach is limited.
Vote shows Upvoted or Downvoted for any HTTP response because toast.promise only fails on network errors. A 404 still shows success.
Footer always says responses are verified by Vex in real time, but the chat route falls back to an unverified stream when Vex errors (route.ts lines 336-355).
Retrieval topK 5 hardcoded here, with minSimilarity 0.3 default in retrieval.ts line 17.
Fallback origin http://localhost:3000.
Base URL falls back to http://localhost:3000.
Base URL falls back to http://localhost:3000.
Redis falls back to redis://localhost:6379. env.ts line 28 sets the same default.
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000.
Widget session tokens never expire. lastActiveAt is updated but never checked.
sendReasoning: true streams model reasoning to the browser, including widget customers. Reasoning can echo the system prompt and chat id. Also line 371 and the widget route line 159.
Public endpoint builds a fetch URL from the request origin, so a spoofed Host header makes the server send a GET to another host.
